column1: Enable CDC in the current Azure SQL Database with {{c1::EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_db;}}
column2:
This enables CDC for the database, not for individual tables. Run it as a member of db_owner on a supported Azure SQL Database tier, then enable each source table you need to capture.
Review source

column1: After enabling CDC on the database, enable a source table through {{c1::sys.sp_cdc_enable_table}}.
column2:
The procedure sets up capture for the named table. Specify its source schema and table name. The gating role controls access to the captured changes.
Review source

column1: For capture instance dbo_Orders, use {{c1::cdc.fn_cdc_get_all_changes_dbo_Orders}} to read change rows within a log sequence number (LSN) range.
column2:
An LSN identifies a position in the transaction log. Use a lower and upper LSN within the retained range so the function can read the changes between them.
Review source

column1: To include before-and-after update rows in a CDC all-changes query, use row filter {{c1::'all update old'}}.
column2:
This filter returns two change rows for an update, one for each image. Use 'all' when you need only the values after the update.
Review source

column1: The CDC metadata column that identifies insert, update, and delete records is {{c1::__$operation}}.
column2:
Read this column to distinguish operation types in the change results. Values 1 and 2 mean delete and insert. Values 3 and 4 mean the before and after rows of an update.
Review source

column1: Enable Change Tracking for YourDatabase with {{c1::ALTER DATABASE [YourDatabase] SET CHANGE_TRACKING = ON;}}
column2:
This enables Change Tracking at database level. Set a retention period that covers consumer outages, and enable tracking separately on each table that a consumer needs.
Review source

column1: After enabling database-level Change Tracking, track Orders with {{c1::ALTER TABLE dbo.Orders ENABLE CHANGE_TRACKING;}}
column2:
The ALTER TABLE command opts Orders into tracking after the database feature is on. Enabling Orders does not also enable tracking for any related tables.
Review source

column1: In isolated-worker C#, monitor Orders using {{c1::[SqlTrigger("[dbo].[Orders]", "SqlConnectionString")]}} on the batch parameter.
column2:
In the trigger attribute, the first string identifies the table and the second names a connection setting. The batch can be IReadOnlyList<SqlChange<Order>> when Order represents the table row.
Review source

column1: With CES preview prerequisites met, enable streaming in the current user database through {{c1::sys.sp_enable_event_stream}}.
column2:
This procedure enables the feature on the current database. For SQL Server 2025, the database must use full recovery and have PREVIEW_FEATURES enabled. You still need to create a stream group.
Review source

column1: Create a CES preview stream group through {{c1::sys.sp_create_event_stream_group}}.
column2:
Use the system procedure to configure the group that will send events to the destination. After creating the group, add the source tables separately.
Review source

column1: Add a table to a CES preview stream group through {{c1::sys.sp_add_object_to_event_stream_group}}.
column2:
Adding a table tells the stream group which object's changes to send. Specify the group name and the table with its schema so SQL can identify the intended source.
Review source

column1: In SQL Server, Change Event Streaming preview cannot be enabled in the same database as {{c1::CDC}}, even for different tables.
column2:
SQL checks for CDC at the database level. Choosing different tables for the two features does not remove this restriction.
Review source

column1: CES preview publishes row-change events in the {{c1::CloudEvents}} format.
column2:
CloudEvents defines a common event envelope. The event data can contain previous and new row values, subject to payload limits and supported data types.
Review source
